resources.string: Plays the metronome for 20 seconds at the current tempo and measures how evenly the clicks are spaced (against the audio clock). You can scroll or switch apps during the test. The result also appears in Diagnostics
At %1$d BPM: mean error %2$s ms · max %3$s ms · %4$d clicks · %5$d glitches
Couldn\'t measure (the audio system gave no timing), try again

Plug a USB-C cable (a data cable, not charge-only) from the piano into the phone and turn the piano on; it shows connected as soon as it\'s plugged in. If the phone asks what to use USB for, choose MIDI. For a Bluetooth piano, search below

If the piano has Bluetooth MIDI, turn it on, press search (up to 10 seconds at a time) and choose its name. The app remembers it but never searches or connects on its own; next time press connect or search when you want
Allow \"Nearby devices\" first. The app uses it only to find the piano, not your location
Bluetooth is off; turn it on and press again
Play the app\'s piano sound when keys are pressed on the real piano
Press any key \"as softly as you can\" %1$d/%2$d
Now press \"as hard as you can\" %1$d/%2$d
The piano sends a fixed velocity, so loud/soft won\'t be a lesson criterion (%1$s)
Press Middle C (the C closest to the middle of the piano) once on the real piano
The note pressed (%1$d) isn\'t a C, try again
No notes yet; press a key on the piano or use the simulator below
Tap to open. Sends simulated MIDI through the same path as a real piano, for testing without one
Pass lesson %1$s at least once first
Not quite: an %2$d-key piano has %1$d %3$s. Try counting from the groups of 2 black keys
· passed with help on %1$d days (not counted yet)
The app names %1$d notes; press each key quickly (on screen or on the piano). A wrong one is shown and asked again at the end
The app shows %1$d notes on the staff; press the matching key (on screen or on the piano)
The metronome counts in 4 clicks, then press any key (or tap the pink pad) with every click. Count aloud too
Not quite, see the highlighted key

Google\'s low-latency audio library · Apache License 2.0

Allow ミミコピ to install apps first (once): press the button below, turn on \"Allow from this source\", then go back
File checked. Wait for the system installer, then press \"Update\" to confirm
The app always backs up on the device before updating. To keep a backup somewhere else too (e.g. Google Drive), press \"Save file first\"
Couldn\'t connect; check the internet and try again

Install failed; your data is all still there
Install cancelled; your data is all still there
A debug build can\'t update itself; use the normal (release) build
Saves all practice data as one JSON file you can keep anywhere. Data lives only on this device, so back up now and then
Automatic backups on the device: %1$d (latest 5 kept)
Can\'t use this file: %1$s. Existing data untouched
The backup from %1$s (version %2$s, %3$d items) will replace all current data. The app backs up the current data first automatically
If something goes wrong or you\'re asked for details, press \"Copy JSON\" and paste it in the chat. There is no personal data in it
Buffer size suggested by the system
App audio stream: %1$d Hz, burst %2$d frames, buffer %3$d frames
Logo and icon: made with an AI image tool for personal use, then redrawn as vectors
Music font Bravura (SIL Open Font License 1.1); text uses the device\'s standard font
Libraries: Jetpack Compose, Room, Kotlin, kotlinx.serialization (Apache License 2.0)
The app has no sheets or lyrics of songs still under copyright. Practice pieces are out of copyright (melodies written from memory, not yet checked against originals)
Key-release sounds and string resonance of the piano
Skill levels compare with this app\'s tests, not music exam grades. Each level\'s criteria and the time split in today\'s plan are starting values still to be tuned from real use
Bluetooth MIDI lags a little more than USB; recalibrate latency when using Bluetooth. With pianos that don\'t report their state, the app can confirm the connection only from keys pressed
Reminders (not wanted yet). On-screen keys take one velocity only, and their timing isn\'t as exact as a real piano (on practice pages they appear only when no MIDI keyboard is connected)

All data stays on this device. The app goes online only when you press \"Check for updates\" (the public GitHub release page) or install the piano sound (downloading sound files), and never sends your data
Choose a piece. Start in \"wait\" mode (the app waits until you press the right note), then move to \"in time\". Practising one section slowly beats looping the whole piece
Pieces use public-domain compositions; some reference editions are Creative Commons. See credits, terms and what was shortened under each piece\'s \"Source and arrangement\"
Tap the last bar of the section
The app plays the hand you aren\'t playing
Starts at about half the target tempo, speeds up after 3 clean rounds in a row and slows after 2 misses in a row, per section and hand
%1$d sets: look at each pair of notes (pink) and say how it moves, then play the whole set in order
Look at the music; starts by itself in %1$d s (or press start)
\"Listen to an example\" repeats the chosen section until you stop it; change tempo with slower/faster
Wait mode: play the note at the cursor, the app waits until it\'s right
Piano sound not installed, so the app can\'t play the other hand or examples (install it on the \"Piano\" tab)
%1$d chords: press the named chord\'s notes together, any inversion or octave, with no extra notes (slash chords need the bass at the bottom)
Change chords along the progression until time runs out; the app counts the right ones. You can hold shared notes
Press every note of the chord together
Not quite, see the highlighted keys (one right inversion)
The app has never closed because of an error
The app has closed because of an error; details are in the Diagnostics file (copy/share above), kept only on this device
No MIDI keyboard connected · press the on-screen keys to try playing along (they disappear once a piano is connected)
Goal: see notes and play them
Come back tomorrow to confirm today\'s steps, or keep practising songs and sections you like

Meet the criteria again so it sticks
The piano is probably off; turn it on and the status returns to Connected by itself
Unplug and replug the cable, or check the connection again
Couldn\'t connect to %1$s; turn the piano on, keep it close and press connect again
No Bluetooth piano found. Check the piano and its Bluetooth are on and not connected to another device, then search again
Off: every note is equally loud however you press; good at first (affects the app\'s sound; with the piano\'s speakers, turn Touch off on the piano)
On: press hard for loud, soft for quiet; for practising touch
